solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tramp's foot worn down going around heart of Alabama?

indicators.note: going around says the shortened foot word encloses the next piece
worn down suggests the word for foot losing its final letter, as if eroded

parts.note: a horse's foot is a hoof

indicators.note: heart of picks out the central letter of the seven-letter state name

explanation.surface: A vagrant's feet, sore from tramping across the Deep South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn down' cuts HOOF to HOO; 'heart of' gives B, the middle of ALABAMA; HOO 'going around' B makes HO-B-O. The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is an American word for a homeless wanderer, which is a synonym of tramp.

clue.text: What horseman does in circling black Scottish region

indicators.note: circling means the phrase goes round the letter for black

parts.note: a horseman rides, so of him one says he rides
B is an abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A rider loops round a dark stretch of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: HE RIDES 'circling' B gives HE-B-RIDES; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrides are island groups off Scotland's west coast, forming a region.

clue.text: Woman, to live like a Queen, disposing of old article

indicators.note: disposing of says letters are removed from the combined words

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
royal means like a queen
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman wants to live like royalty but gets rid of an old piece.
explanation.walkthrough: BE + ROYAL gives BEROYAL; 'disposing of' O and A leaves BERYL.
explanation.definitionFit: Beryl is a female first name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Lad following racecourse information and activity

indicators.note: following places the word for lad after the racecourse term

parts.note: the going is the state of the ground reported at a racecourse
a lad is a son

explanation.surface: A young stable lad keeps track of the latest news from the track.
explanation.walkthrough: THE GOING, in British horse racing, is the official report on how soft or firm the turf is.
explanation.definitionFit: Goings-on are happenings or events, often suspicious ones, so busy activity fits.

clue.text: Marine stuff to go in road after storm

indicators.note: in puts the urinating word inside the scrambled letters
after a storm the letters of the word are scattered

parts.note: to go can mean to urinate, to wee

explanation.surface: Seaweed has to be shifted from the road after a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after storm' makes OARD, and 'in' puts the slang word for urinating inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarweed is a large brown kelp of the shore, a marine plant material.

clue.text: Primitive hominid that's carved a remnant (handle)

indicators.note: carved suggests material cut and reshaped, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A prehistoric human whittled a leftover scrap into a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: An early extinct species of human, so a primitive member of the hominids.

clue.text: Sound happier, perhaps, admitting initially to having no view

indicators.note: admitting means letting the next letter inside

parts.note: a happier person might sigh less

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone sounds more cheerful while confessing they have no opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'view' looks like an opinion but means sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sightless means blind, unable to see, so having no view of anything.

clue.text: Spanish city keeping up this festival

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the city name is read from the bottom

parts.note: Leon is a city in northern Spain

explanation.surface: A Spanish city keeps up its celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this festival' refers to the season the puzzle appeared around, Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is another word for Christmas, the festival the clue points to.

clue.text: Skin treatment prepared by dermal upstarts?

indicators.note: prepared, as a remedy is made up, signals the letters being reworked

explanation.surface: A remedy for the skin is concocted by cocky young dermatologists.
explanation.definitionFit: A poultice of mustard spread on cloth, laid on the skin as a traditional remedy.

clue.text: Wise person was positioned around the forefront

indicators.note: around means the past-tense word encloses the next piece

parts.note: sat means was placed or seated
the van is the vanguard, the forefront

explanation.surface: A sage was seated at the very front.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a learned scholar, someone of great knowledge.

clue.text: Returned mailbag after crash in notorious location

indicators.note: after a crash, the letters of the two words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A postbag sent back after a plane crash at some infamous spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word looks like a reversal signal but is part of the fodder, rearranged 'after crash'; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch of Atlantic off Florida is infamous for legends of vanishing ships and aircraft.

clue.text: Entrance one with touch of luxury in lacy stuff

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in says the first letter of luxury goes inside the fabric word

parts.note: net is an openwork lacy fabric

indicators.note: a touch of a word means just its first letter

explanation.surface: A doorway draped with a luxurious lace curtain.
explanation.walkthrough: NET with L (first letter of 'luxury') 'in' it gives NLET, after I for 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow entrance of water from the sea, or any way in.

clue.text: Story's a brief comment about City Director

indicators.note: about means the note word goes round the next two pieces

parts.note: a note is a short written comment
EC is the postcode area for the City of London

explanation.surface: A tale that turns out to be just a quick remark about a City of London executive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes NECDOTE. The City is London's financial district, whose postcode letters are the crossword standard; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing tale about a real incident, a type of story.

clue.text: Passage runs into bar

indicators.note: into says the abbreviation goes inside the word for bar

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A corridor leads straight into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but means 'except'; R for runs goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a passage taken from a longer text or piece of music.

clue.text: Roundabouts with zero application left to impede vehicles

indicators.note: to impede means to get in the way, so the pieces sit inside the vehicles word

parts.note: cars are vehicles
O looks like zero
use means application, as in putting to use

explanation.surface: Traffic circles with no applications left blocking cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundabouts' looks like British traffic junctions; here they are fairground rides.
explanation.definitionFit: Merry-go-rounds at a fairground are carousels, also called roundabouts in Britain.

clue.text: Throw shade over boat in hideaway

indicators.note: in places the boat word inside the hideaway word

parts.note: a den is a private hiding place or retreat
an ark is a boat, as Noah's

explanation.surface: Someone shades a boat moored in a secret hiding place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw shade' now also means to insult, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: To darken something is to make it dimmer, as shade cast over it would.

clue.text: Maxim, rather outdated, describing circus rings?

parts.note: a saw is an old proverb or maxim
dusty means stale or old-fashioned

explanation.surface: An old saying, a bit dated, about circus rings.
explanation.walkthrough: Circus rings are traditionally floored with sawdust, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Circus rings are strewn with wood shavings, so the adjective for covered in them fits.

clue.text: Doctor leading surgery in (informal) call

indicators.note: leading puts the doctor's abbreviation in front

parts.note: an op is an operation, that is, surgery

explanation.surface: A doctor heading an operation pops in for a casual house call.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in is to pay a casual, unannounced visit, an informal call.

clue.text: Rain storms enveloping range and falls

indicators.note: enveloping means the scrambled letters wrap round the cooker
storms here is a verb, the letters rushing into a new order

parts.note: an Aga is a make of kitchen range, a cooking stove

explanation.surface: Rainstorms sweep across a mountain range and its waterfalls.
explanation.walkthrough: RAIN 'storms' to NIRA, 'enveloping' AGA. An Aga is a heavy British cast-iron cooker; 'range' looks like mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous waterfall on the US–Canada border, the Falls.

clue.text: Apparently has one advanced problem with words

parts.note: ap. is a dictionary abbreviation for apparently
taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I
A is a standard abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: Someone seems to have a language difficulty that is getting worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphasia is a brain disorder that impairs the ability to speak or understand language.

clue.text: Move on once relative has secured Volume One

indicators.note: has secured means holding the next pieces inside

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
A means one, as in a single

explanation.surface: An aunt has nabbed the first volume of a set.
explanation.definitionFit: This old exclamation means begone, an archaic command to go away.

clue.text: Swede with routine articles, including sack

parts.note: a rut is a dull fixed routine

indicators.note: including says the two articles enclose the sack word

parts.note: A and A, two indefinite articles
a bag is a sack

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian with a dull routine and a sackful of belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' is not a Scandinavian but the root vegetable, called rutabaga in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Rutabaga is the American name for the root vegetable the British call a swede.

clue.text: Nobleman's study, say, leading to degree

indicators.note: leading to puts the den word before the next piece

parts.note: a lair is a private den, and a den can be a study

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's study is the first step to an academic degree.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. A laird is a Scottish landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish landowner of the gentry, loosely a nobleman.

clue.text: Asimov, say, is current around America

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: around puts the current abbreviation round the next letter

parts.note: AC stands for alternating current

explanation.surface: Science-fiction writer Asimov is electric across America.
explanation.walkthrough: Isaac Asimov was the science-fiction author; 'say' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The author's first name serves as an example of that given name.

clue.text: Declined to dismiss umpire being exploited

indicators.note: to dismiss means to send off, so the official is removed

parts.note: to have refused is to have declined
a ref is a referee or umpire

explanation.surface: A batsman declined to send off the umpire who was being exploited.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken advantage of is being used, as a person can feel used.

clue.text: Nothing mandates way Fens should be treated

indicators.note: treated here means processed, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: An official order governs how the Fens wetlands are to be managed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are low-lying marshland in eastern England. The answer is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang phrase means nothing whatsoever, a euphemism for a coarser expression.

clue.text: Presentation of anagram is arranged in time

indicators.note: in puts the two pieces inside the time word

parts.note: a day is a period of time
taken as written
arr. is the musical abbreviation for arranged

explanation.surface: A crossword setter explains how an anagram is arranged in time.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on itself: an anagram's letters are shown in a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: An anagram's fodder appears scrambled, so its presentation is a state of muddle and confusion.

clue.text: Painful account — hardly heartless

indicators.note: heartless means the inner letters of the word are removed, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A painful story, hardly a heartless one.
explanation.definitionFit: Achy describes something that aches, so it is sore or painful.
